To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated that domain randomization and GAN based data augmentation enables training a robust near real-time Mask-RCNN detector in a simulated environment using very little real world data.

a) domain randomization and GAN translation enable robust translation of synthetic data to the real world, b) a combination of the GAN translated and original synthetic images can achieve greater than 0% mean average precision in object detection, c) a combination of synthetic and GAN translated data can be trained in near real-time (i.e., in a matter of hours).
a combination of domain randomization techniques and GAN translation enables robust translation of simulated images to the real-world domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following research questions: How does domain randomization and GAN translation affect the performance of an object detection model in a real world setting?
the development of a novel framework for training a near real-time Mask-RCNN detector entirely in simulation using domain randomization and GAN.
the problem of training an industrial object detection system in the absence of large amounts of real world data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method can be used to train a near-realtime object detection network, entirely using synthetic images.

the proposed approach is capable of achieving near real-time object detection and classification of industrial electric parts in a simulated environment, without requiring access to large-scale real world datasets.
the use of domain randomization with generative adversarial refinement of synthetic images can be used to train near real-time object detection models, with high accuracy and robustness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of domain randomization with a generative adversarial translation network enables robust object detection and classification in a simulated environment, with a high degree of generalization to the real world.

we have demonstrated that the combination of domain randomization, and GAN translation of synthetic images is an effective approach to train an object detector in a simulated environment, without the need of large scale real world data.
the proposed method can be a viable solution for training object detection networks for real world applications, when the amount of real world labelled data is limited.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed methodology is capable of achieving a high level of performance on a real world industrial object detection task, without the need for any real world data.
a combination of domain randomization, GAN and a few hundred unlabelled real world images can be used to train a robust object detector in a simulated environment.

a combination of domain randomization, GAN translation and object detection training can enable robust object detection in the real world without the need for real data, which is often difficult to obtain in industrial settings.
